macro: The FOMC begins its two-day meeting today, with futures pricing roughly a 90-93% chance of a 25-basis-point hike to 3.75%-4.00% when the decision lands Wednesday at 2pm ET. August headline CPI ran 3.35% year-over-year with core CPI at 2.45%, still above the Fed's 2% target, while the 10-year Treasury yield broke above 5% on Monday for the first time since October 2023 as a global bond selloff compounded oil-driven inflation fears. Middle East supply risk remains the wildcard: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has stayed shut since last week's drone strikes, and Gulf-Iran talks over Strait of Hormuz shipping have stalled. The date to watch: Wednesday, September 16, 2pm ET, for the FOMC rate decision and updated dot plot.

mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 6.76% for the week ended September 10, up from 6.71% the prior week. Combined with home prices still rising year-over-year, that keeps affordability pressured even as for-sale inventory has climbed to its highest level in over a decade.
personal_finance_deep_dive: The personal savings rate fell to 3.0% in July, down from levels above 6% just two years earlier, even as disposable income has continued to rise in nominal terms. The gap reflects inflation-driven cost pressure in categories households can't easily cut, particularly housing, which pushes more of each month's cash flow toward current consumption and credit rather than savings. Renters and lower-income households tend to be the most exposed, since they have the least cushion to absorb rising costs without drawing down savings or adding debt. A savings rate this low, sustained over multiple quarters, has historically preceded a slowdown in consumer spending growth.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Fidelity's retirement accounts crossed a record 769,000 401(k) millionaires in the second quarter, up 19% from 654,000 in the first quarter — the largest one-quarter jump since late 2023. The gains reflect two forces working together: a rising equity market and sustained high contribution rates, with combined worker-and-match 401(k) savings rates running near record levels this year. The lesson scales down: a worker earning $70,000 who contributes 15% of pay, captures a full employer match, and holds through market swings rather than trying to time entries and exits is following the same mechanism that built these balances — consistent contribution and time in the market, not stock selection.
